title: DTEND/DUE and DURATION Are Mutually Exclusive and DURATION Is Positive and Valid

citations.verbatim_quote: ; Either 'dtend' or 'duration' MAY appear in ; a 'eventprop', but 'dtend' and 'duration' ; MUST NOT occur in the same 'eventprop'.

; Either 'due' or 'duration' MAY appear in ; a 'todoprop', but 'due' and 'duration' ; MUST NOT occur in the same 'todoprop'. ; If 'duration' appear in a 'todoprop', ; then 'dtstart' MUST also appear in ; the same 'todoprop'.
Purpose: This property specifies a positive duration of time.
When the "DURATION" property relates to a "DTSTART" property that is specified as a DATE value, then the "DURATION" property MUST be specified as a "dur-day" or "dur-week" value.

statement: A VEVENT never carries both DTEND and DURATION, and a VTODO never carries both DUE and DURATION; whenever DURATION is present, DTSTART is also present, DURATION is a valid strictly positive RFC 5545 duration, and if DTSTART is a DATE value then DURATION uses day or week units only.
rationale: RFC 5545 Sections 3.6.1 and 3.6.2 forbid DTEND (resp. DUE) and DURATION in the same component and require DTSTART whenever DURATION appears in a VTODO; Section 3.8.2.5 requires DURATION to specify a positive duration and restricts DATE-anchored components to dur-day or dur-week values.
